nodes.name: PGM-free catalyst synthesis
nodes.procedure: High-temperature pyrolysis of nitrogen precursors (cyanamide and polyaniline), iron precursor (FeCl3) and carbon support (Black Pearl 2000) combined with a pore-forming agent (ZnCl2), followed by acid leaching, magnetic separation using a permanent magnet and a second pyrolysis.
nodes.source_text: The PGM-free catalyst used in this paper was prepared by high-temperature pyrolysis of nitrogen precursors (cyanamide and polyaniline), iron precursor (FeCl3) and carbon support (Black Pearl 2000) combined with a pore-forming agent (ZnCl2), followed by acid leaching, magnetic separation using a permanent magnet and a second pyrolysis (15, 16).

nodes.name: Catalyst ink preparation
nodes.procedure: Catalyst inks were prepared by mixing 30 mg of the catalyst with various amounts of ionomer dispersions in a solvent containing water and isopropanol and sonicating in an ultrasonic bath for 4 to 5 h.

nodes.name: Hot-pressed MEA fabrication
nodes.procedure: The catalyst ink was hand-brushed onto a Nafion® NR211 membrane at ~80 °C to make a 5 cm² electrode with a catalyst loading of ca. 4.8 mg/cm². Then, MEA was obtained by hot-pressing a gas diffusion layer (GDL, 29BC, Ion Power) onto the cathode catalyst layer and a 0.3 mgPt cm-2 anode (a gas diffusion electrode, GDE, Fuel Cell Store) on the other side of the membrane at 120 °C for 5 min using a pressure of ca. 5.3 MPa. PTFE gaskets were used to control the compression of MEAs in fuel cell hardware to ca. 75% to 80% of its original thickness.

nodes.name: Non hot-pressed MEA fabrication
nodes.procedure: The anode GDE was first hot-pressed to one side a Nafion® NR211 membrane at 120 °C, 5.3 MPa for 5 min. The catalyst ink was then brush-painted to the cathode side of the membrane at ~80 °C to achieve a same catalyst loading of ca. 4.8 mg/cm². In both cases, the MEAs were assembled by adding GDLs on top of the cathode CL. PTFE gaskets were used to control the compression of MEAs in fuel cell hardware to ca. 75% to 80% of its original thickness.

nodes.description: H₂-air fuel cell performance comparison of hot-pressed vs not hot-pressed MEAs using different ionomers

ionomer_types.value: Nafion D521 (35 wt%), Aquivion D72 (35 wt%)

nodes.source_text: Figure 3 shows the polarization plots with the cathodes fabricated by the CCM method with and without hot-pressing. It can be observed that hot-pressed MEAs suffer from performance loss at high current densities due to higher mass transport resistance... MEA fabricated without the hot-pressing show improved performance at both ohmic and mass transport regions.

nodes.description: H₂-air fuel cell performance with varying Nafion D521 content (25-55 wt%), not hot-pressed
nodes.source_text: Figure 4 shows the polarization plots of MEAs containing different Nafion D521 contents. Fuel cell performance at the kinetic region increases with an increase in the ionomer loading. When Nafion content was 25 wt%, the kinetic and ohmic performance is much lower...

nodes.description: 2D contour analysis of ionomer EW and content effects on key performance metrics
nodes.source_text: Figure 5 shows the dependency of fuel cell performance on the EW and the content of ionomer... the best fuel cell performance at 0.65 V is achieved at moderate ionomer loadings, 35 wt% or 45 wt%, with all tested ionomers... Aquivion D83 with an EW value of 830 g mol⁻¹ yields the most balanced fuel cell performance.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM micrographs show the PGM-free catalyst layer (CL) thickness of approximately 100 μm, much thicker than Pt/C anode CL at 10 μm. Not hot-pressed CL is 30-40 μm thicker than hot-pressed CL.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1 shows an SEM micrograph of the cross-section of a typical MEA with a PGM-free cathode and a Pt/C anode. The thickness of the PGM-free CL is approximately 100 μm, much thicker than the Pt/C CL at the anode, which is approximately 10 μm.

properties.description: Cross-sectional image of membrane electrode assembly (MEA)

nodes.characterization_summary: Oxygen-free cyclic voltammograms of PGM-free cathodes recorded from 0 to 1.0 V vs. RHE at 20 mV/s scan rate show double layer capacitance increases with ionomer content. ECSA estimated using constant capacitance of 30 μF/cm² increases with ionomer content and EW, correlating with kinetic performance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The oxygen-free cyclic voltammograms for the PGM-free cathodes were measured on a CHI 760d potentiostat... The cyclic voltammograms were recorded from 0 to 1.0 V vs. RHE at a scan rate of 20 mV/s. A constant capacitance of 30 μF/cm² was employed to estimate the electrochemical surface area (ECSA) of PGM-free catalyst in the cathode.
